ZH.Who — Round 2, grok's Picks

A different source. Every face here was named by grok, asked separately for each direction and told which fonts the last round used and that they were rejected. Cards 01–10 are the Need for Speed: Underground 2 read — and grok went somewhere the last round never did: graffiti, JDM display, neon tube and stencil rather than wide squared techno. Cards 11–20 are cyberpunk, and grok's instinct there was narrow, not wide — condensed industrial, terminal grotesque, stencil. Two picks come from outside Google Fonts. Z, H and W each toggle case independently. Every font is SIL Open Font License or Apache 2.0.

Substitution. grok's tenth pick was VG5000, also from Velvetyne — a modular digital display face. I could not obtain it: its GitHub repository is empty and Velvetyne's page exposes no download link. This is the nearest thing on hand — a squared terminal mono with a boxed @, in the same machine-signage register.

Small-size risk: Low, but light. Monospaced, so the dot in ZH.Who gets a full character width.

Production files are in this folder as NN-slug.svg. They are plain outlined SVG — open in Illustrator, Inkscape, Affinity or Cricut Design Space, or hand them to a printer as-is. Each file holds exactly two paths, one gold and one red, so colour separation is already done.

The keyline toggle previews a bone-coloured sticker border. Most print shops generate the actual die-cut contour themselves from the artwork outline, so send the flat files unless yours asks for a cut path.
